titleEn: Stop Your Feet, Look Both Ways, Hand Up!

pages.text: "A falling leaf!" Careless Duri tilted their head, watching it. Rainbow Class was walking to the river with Teacher Bau. They reached the village road in front of the kindergarten.
Duri jumped to catch the leaf. It fluttered across the road. Those feet followed only the leaf.
Without looking ahead, Duri stepped toward the road. Teacher Bau quickly caught their shoulders. "Duri, wait!" Duri's toes stopped at the edge.
Just then, a bicycle rang its bell and passed. Duri's heart thumped. Duri tugged the neckerchief knot. Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, held Duri's hand tightly.
Teacher Bau pointed to a white line at the roadside. "This is where we stop. Put your toes right before the line." Duri placed both toes there side by side.
"Stop your feet, look both ways, hand up!" Teacher Bau showed each step. Duri copied: look left, look right, hand high! "Stop your feet, look both ways, hand up!"
No cars or bicycles were coming. Teacher Bau held Duri's hand and led. With the other hand high, Duri crossed carefully. Reaching the other side, Duri jumped.
"I crossed without watching the leaf!" Duri called. "Yes, you watched the road instead." Teacher Bau bent down and smiled. Duri's shoulders lifted proudly.
On the way back, Duri stopped at the white line first. "One, stop your feet! Two, turn your head and look both ways! Three, one hand up, the other holding Teacher, and cross!" Mio raised a hand too.

By the yard gate, Teacher Bau hugged Duri. However interesting something flying may be, feet must stop first at the road. Waving the leaf Duri had found, Duri said, "Stop your feet, look both ways, hand up!"
